metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after spikes or rebounds; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; apply a “cool-down” factor: reduce forecast by 10–20% for 2–5 day horizons post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons; if forecast is >20% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.
- Sentiment history is uniformly neutral (0.00) across all examples — no sentiment-driven bias observed; ignore sentiment for correction unless sentiment >0.3 or < -0.3.
- Model underestimates prices in late forecast periods (e.g., 25–30 days) — especially when true values dip below 30–40% of initial forecast range; apply a “tail correction” by adding 2–5% to forecast if true outcome is below 35% of 30-day average.
- No horizon-specific lag error detected — forecasts are generally aligned with true values within 1–3 days, but drifts occur after 7–10 days; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 1–3% for forecasts beyond 7 days.
